MESSAGE:
Dear Acme Cloud Services,

Thank you for your email regarding renewal of our contract, currently running from 1 November 2025 to 31 October 2026, and your proposal of a 12% price increase to Rs 2,68,000/month.

Under Clause 8.2 of our agreement, renewal price increases are capped at 7% unless both parties agree otherwise in writing. A 12% increase exceeds this cap and, per our internal procurement policy, increases above 10% cannot be accepted as proposed and must instead be negotiated down or opened to competitive bidding. We are therefore unable to accept the 12% increase as presented.

Separately, per Clause 4.1/4.2, your services fell below the 99.9% monthly uptime SLA in May (99.42%) and July (99.61%), entitling us to service credits of Rs 10,000 per month, totaling Rs 20,000, which have not yet been claimed. We request these credits be applied to offset any renewal costs.

We value our relationship with Acme and are open to renewing for a further 12 months (per Clause 8.1) on the following counter-terms: an increase within the 7% contractual cap, i.e. up to approximately Rs 2,14,000/month, with the Rs 20,000 in outstanding SLA credits applied against the first invoice(s) of the renewed term.

We have also received competitive market quotes in a similar range to our proposed counter-offer, which support our position that a 12% increase is not commercially justified at this time.
